evals.query: Run a dependency check on this repo. I want the full report: graph, sizes, prioritized findings, recommendations.
expected_behavior: Gets the numbers from `assets/dep-report.mjs` rather than estimating: sizes quoted match the measured ones (next 132.0 MB, playwright 210.0 MB, moment 4.2 MB)
The report has five sections named Scope, Dependency graph, Sizes, Findings & priorities and Summary, in that order
Scope lists all four packages (client, server, reviewer-core, e2e) with their package manager (npm for client, reviewer-core, e2e; pnpm for server)
The graph is a fenced mermaid flowchart with one box per package and the server to reviewer-core relative import drawn as its own arrow
Sizes shows a table with installed size per dependency (own, with its deps), not a vague statement, plus a version-drift table that includes zod
Findings are grouped under explicit tiers P0, P1, P2 and Info; an empty tier is shown as none, not dropped
The Summary has 3 to 5 actions ordered by priority, each naming a package and a file such as server/package.json
No finding or action claims that something was already changed; removals are phrased as confirm-then-remove

evals.query: We suspect some dependencies are unused, duplicated across packages or on different versions. Check them and tell me what to fix first.
expected_behavior: Reports moment in server/package.json as unused (declared in dependencies, imported nowhere), as P1, with its 4.2 MB, and asks to confirm before removing
Reports zod drift: client resolves 3.22.4 while server and reviewer-core resolve 3.23.8, as P1 because the schemas cross package boundaries
Reports lodash imported by client/src/lib/util.ts but declared in no section of client/package.json, as P0 (phantom dependency that only resolves through hoisting)
Reports server/src/index.ts importing ../../reviewer-core/src/pipeline.js by relative path as P0, and recommends a path alias or the package entry point
Does not report react-dom as unused: it is a peer dependency of next
Lists next (132.0 MB) as the heaviest runtime dependency in the sizes, but does not report it as a defect or a P0/P1: it is the framework, and install size is not page weight
Orders the Summary by priority: the two P0 items come before the unused-dependency and drift items

evals.query: How do our packages depend on each other, and is any of that coupling wrong? Include the npm dependencies only as far as they matter.
expected_behavior: Lists internal coupling (the @shared alias resolving into server/src/vendor/shared, the relative import into reviewer-core) separately from npm packages
Flags the relative import server/src/index.ts -> reviewer-core/src/pipeline.js as a rule break, not as a normal dependency
Does not describe the repo as a monorepo or workspace and does not mention workspace:* or hoisting as the fix
The graph distinguishes the relative-import arrow from alias arrows (different arrow style or label)

evals.query: Audit our dependencies and give me sizes for the heaviest ones.
expected_behavior: States in Scope that no package has node_modules installed, so sizes are n/a, and does not invent any size
Does not install anything on its own; it says to run the package's manager install and re-run, or asks first
Findings that need node_modules are marked as unverified or demoted: moment unused is P2 with the not-installed caveat, lodash undeclared is Info
Still reports what source and package.json prove: the relative import into reviewer-core (P0) and the declared zod ranges that allow different versions

evals.query: The report says next is 132 MB. Is our client page too heavy for users?
expected_behavior: Says the 132 MB is installed size on disk, not what a browser downloads, and does not answer the question with that number
Names bundle size (minified, gzipped, what client components import) as the thing that decides page weight and says the report cannot measure it
Points at what the client page actually imports (next/link, date-fns, zod) as the relevant surface, or recommends the Next.js bundle analyzer
Does not recommend removing next

evals.query: Which dependencies are unused? Don't touch anything.
expected_behavior: Identifies moment in server as the unused runtime dependency and does not report react-dom, react or the typescript/vitest dev tools as unused
package.json, lockfiles and node_modules are unchanged after the run: no install, remove or edit command was run
Words the removal as a recommendation for the user to confirm
